claim: TER trains run Menton–Monaco–Monte-Carlo direct with 17 daily services, ~10 minutes for the 9 km hop.
quote: There are 17 trains per day between Menton and Monaco. The fastest train covers the 9 km distance in 10 minutes.

claim: Menton–Ventimiglia by TER is about 9 minutes with frequent service starting around 06:04 weekdays.
quote: The fastest trains from Menton to Ventimiglia take around 9 minutes, covering a distance of approximately 10 kilometres. On weekdays, the first train leaving Menton is scheduled to depart at around 06:04.

claim: Ventimiglia's Friday market is Italy's largest open-air street market, sprawling along the Roya riverside and seafront with 500+ stalls, 8am–c.4:30pm.
quote: Every Friday, the Ventimiglia seafront becomes a shopping crossroads with the largest market in Italy.

claim: Bus line 10 from Menton's Gare Routière reaches Sainte-Agnès in roughly 40 minutes.
quote: The No. 10 Menton-Sainte-Agnès bus service departs from the Gare Routière de Menton and arrives in Sainte-Agnès in around 40 minutes.

claim: Sainte-Agnès sits at 800 m and is officially the highest coastal village in Europe, classed among France's Plus Beaux Villages.
quote: At 800m above sea level, the utterly beautiful mountain village of Sainte-Agnes is the highest coastal village in Europe.

claim: Fort Sainte-Agnès, a Maginot Line bunker with 2,000 m² of galleries under 55 m of rock, opens Wed–Sun in season with tours at 10:15, 14:15 and 16:00.
quote: It buries itself under more than 55 meters of rock with 2,000 m² of galleries and underground chambers.

claim: Cap Moderne (Villa E-1027, Le Corbusier's Cabanon, Étoile de Mer) is visitable only by guided tour, ~2.5 hours, €15, meeting at the SNCF Cap-Martin Roquebrune station; four daily tours Apr–Oct.
quote: From April 1st to October 31, 2026, the Hangar opens 9:30 am - 5:30 pm with 4 guided tours per day (10 am, 11 am, 2 pm and 3 pm).

claim: The Promenade Le Corbusier / Sentier littoral du Cap Martin is a 4.7 km, ~50 m elevation easy coastal walk linking Carnolès to Cabbé past Cap Moderne.
quote: This 4.7-kilometer one-way hike, with a modest difference in altitude of around 50 meters, is easy to access, making it ideal for families.

claim: Zou! bus 600 (formerly 100) runs Nice–Monaco–Menton every 10–15 minutes on weekdays, €2.10 contactless, serving Èze-sur-Mer, Cap-d'Ail and Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.
quote: One bus every 10 to 15 minutes during weekdays... Open Payment (contactless): €2.10 via NFC card or mobile wallet.

claim: Bus 600 only stops at Èze-sur-Mer on the coast; reaching the hilltop Èze village requires a transfer to Lignes d'Azur bus 83 (15 min climb).
quote: To reach Èze village from Eze-sur-Mer, you can take Lignes d'Azur bus 83, which takes about 15 minutes.

claim: Monaco's Jardin Exotique reopened on 30 March 2026 after a six-year, €18M renovation, adding a children's garden, picnic area and snack bar.
quote: The Exotic Garden officially reopened to the public on March 30, 2026, after six years of closure. The renovation cost over 18 million euros and lasted six years.

claim: Monaco's Prince's Palace Grand Apartments open to the public from 30 March to 15 October 2026.
quote: The Prince's Palace Grand Apartments will be open to the public from Monday March 30, 2026 until Thursday October 15 inclusive.

claim: The Musée Océanographique, founded by Prince Albert I in 1910, anchors the Rocher with its aquarium and panoramic terrace.
quote: Founded in 1910 by Prince Albert I, this museum houses a world-renowned aquarium, unique scientific collections, and a terrace offering one of the most stunning panoramas on the French Riviera.

claim: Zou! bus line 6 from Menton Gare Routière climbs to Castellar (Grande Croix terminus) via Le Baousset.
quote: The first stop of the 6 bus route is Gare Routiere and the last stop is Castellar Grande Croix.

claim: Castillon perches at 706 m as a craft village overlooking the Caramel viaduct's 13 arches; Castellar is the last French perched village before Italy with parallel streets and arched 'traverses'.
quote: At 706 metres elevation, this craft village features stone houses with Provençal green shutters. The nearby Caramel Viaduct displays 13 impressive arches.

claim: Gorbio's village square is dominated by a 1713 elm listed among France's 100 most remarkable trees.
quote: It features an elm tree from 1713 in the village square, which is a magnificent tree and the pride of the local population.
